chunks: Ibn al-Walid, from al-Saffar, from al-Yaqtini, from al-Ja'fari, who said:
Al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: The Will is from the attributes of actions. So whoever asserts that Allah never stopped willing and intending is not a monotheist.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between divine Will as an attribute of action versus essence in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that divine Will (al-Mashi'ah) is an attribute of action (Sifat al-Fi'l) rather than essence (Sifat al-Dhat), distinguishing it from eternal attributes like Knowledge. This distinction safeguards Tawhid by rejecting the notion that God’s will is a static, co-eternal entity, a key point in Shia theological debates against the Mu'tazila and Ash'aris regarding whether divine attributes are identical to His essence or distinct.
